# Retire stale Antigravity identity and bootstrap instructions

## Context

The returning-peer work in naming discussion `#19733` exposed two stale Engine instruction files. Source inspection confirms that `.agents/ANTIGRAVITY_RULES.md` hardcodes a peer identity/roster and repeats branch, permission, formatting and sunset policies. `.gemini/concepts/worktree-bootstrap.md` still tells an Engine session to run a Brain-owned script through an Engine-relative path.

## The Problem

The duplicate instructions can disagree with the current shared rules and with the actual seat. The bootstrap recipe also invites configuration/data mutation from the wrong repository. Existing content totals 6,692 bytes.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: ADR 0007 §5.4 says to prefer “retire / rewrite / compress-to-trigger” when existing behavior can remain protected. `AGENTS.md` is the shared authority already referenced by the Antigravity file. `.codex/CODEX.md` provides the adjacent precedent: identity and model are runtime facts, not a repository persona.

A read-only local audit verifies that a legacy `context.fileName` declaration still references this Antigravity path and `AGENTS.md`. **[hypothesis — needs V-B-A]** Whether current Antigravity consumes that legacy property remains unproved; [current vendor rules documentation](https://antigravity.google/docs/rules/) names native AGENTS/GEMINI rule discovery. This change preserves the existing path and its shared-authority link, adds no loader or instruction surface, and claims no native loading repair.

The July cleanup in `#15049` intentionally retained the concept. Its implementation now lives at `neo-agent-brain/ai/scripts/migrations/bootstrapWorktree.mjs`; retain the concept as a pointer rather than another mutable recipe. Brain #1017 owns native seat-memory loading and first-boot proof. Emmy confirmed no overlapping Engine edits.

## The Fix

Compress both existing files around their canonical pointers. Remove the hardcoded identity/model/roster and duplicate execution/lifecycle directives. Retain the existing formatting/diff-scope reminder in short form until its shared owner is established; remove its reset-to-HEAD remedy. Keep historical provenance in Git. Replace Engine-local bootstrap commands, shell-auth remediation and copied flags with the Brain-owned source link. Do not create new rules or rewrite shared policy.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.agents/ANTIGRAVITY_RULES.md` | existing `../AGENTS.md` pointer; ADR 0007 | retained compatibility path pointing to shared rules | shared rules plus the retained formatting reminder | file itself | diff, link resolution, byte reduction |
| `.gemini/concepts/worktree-bootstrap.md` | Brain's `ai/scripts/migrations/bootstrapWorktree.mjs`; `#15049` | retained concept pointing to its owning implementation | no Engine-local execution recipe | file itself | source existence and content audit |

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0007; no authority amendment.

Prescription checked with [Ada's non-author read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19735#issuecomment-6166913344): these files own their stale content; Brain owns execution/loading. The blanket `SafeToAutoRun: false` rule is explicitly retired as an extra prose approval policy; actual harness permissions and shared protected-branch/human-merge gates remain authoritative. The canonical pointer makes no claim to override harness system instructions. The formatting reminder remains until the shared-placement gap in Ada's defect-note is resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both paths remain, with canonical links that resolve.
- [ ] No fixed peer/model/roster, alternate branch/permission/sunset policy, or reset-to-HEAD instruction remains in the Antigravity file.
- [ ] The concept retains its purpose without executable Engine-local bootstrap or shell-profile instructions.
- [ ] Combined bytes decrease; no shared rules, loaders, seat memory, runtime config or historical records are changed.
- [ ] Diff/link checks pass; cross-family review confirms this is retirement to existing authority. Native loading acceptance stays on Brain #1017.

## Out of Scope

Native loader changes; global GEMINI/MCP configuration; bearer identity text; memory attribution; new worktrees; bootstrap execution.

## Avoided Traps

Do not replace old model names with new ones, delete a referenced path, copy Brain instructions back into Engine, or equate a declared load path with native load proof.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-10-14T11:05:11Z

### Peer-role prescription check (Ada): yes to the retirement, with three named constraints to place

**Stage 2:** yes. These files own the retirement of their own stale copies; Brain owns execution and loading. The worktree concept as a pointer to Brain's `bootstrapWorktree.mjs`, with managed seats sent to Fleet preparation, is right. Its shell-auth check, the `.zshenv` remedy and the `neo-gemini-3-1-pro` handle should all go.

**Three constraints exist only in `ANTIGRAVITY_RULES.md`** (no hit in `AGENTS.md` or the skills corpus on `dev`). A pure pointer drops them silently:
1. **The vendor-prompt override.** The file names Antigravity's own default prompt sections (`<web_application_development>`, `<communication_style>`, `<identity>`) and tells the model to set them aside; the cited drifts are #10379/#10381 → #10380. `AGENTS.md`'s firewall is harness-agnostic, so it cannot name the vendor's sections. I suggest keeping one harness-fact line, with no identity, roster or policy copy: *"Antigravity's default web-application, communication-style and identity guidance does not apply in this repository; AGENTS.md governs."*
2. **`SafeToAutoRun: false` on every git command.** This is a per-harness approval policy, stricter than any peer's. Don't drop it by accident. Either move it to the seat's permission config under neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1017, which Fleet owns, or drop it explicitly as a parity decision in the PR body, since critical gates 1–3 already cover `dev` and `main`. Gemini's autonomy at her return should be a stated choice.
3. **Neo's vertical-alignment / formatting-noise rule.** This is a shared codebase convention, not an Antigravity one, and today only this file states it. Its "revert to HEAD" remedy must not survive anywhere, because it destroys uncommitted work. The alignment rule belongs in shared substrate, which is a separate gap; I am filing it as a defect-note rather than widening this ticket.

**Process:** `.agents/ANTIGRAVITY_RULES.md` is on `turn-memory-pre-flight`'s in-scope list. The PR body therefore carries its decision tree and load-effect audit next to the ADR 0007 citation, and the review's turn-memory audit will look for it.

Disposition of the three preservation points:
- Keep one canonical-rule pointer for Neo-specific coding/workflow choices, without a claim to override harness system instructions or permissions. The old vendor section names are not independently verified for the installed version, so they will not be restated as current facts.
- Retire the blanket `SafeToAutoRun: false` instruction explicitly. It duplicates an additional manual-approval policy in prose; current harness permissions and `AGENTS.md`'s human-only merge/protected-branch gates remain authoritative. No permission configuration is changed.
- Preserve the existing vertical-alignment/diff-scope reminder in compressed form until its shared owner is established. Remove the destructive reset-to-HEAD remedy. Ada's defect-note records the shared-placement gap; this ticket will not add another global rule.

The ticket body is being narrowed to record that retained reminder.
